newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM agrees to parliamentary bank probe - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM agrees to parliamentary bank probe - agency.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Tuesday agreed with the chairman of parliament, Milos Zeman, to set up a parliamentary commission to investigate the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s., the CTK agency said.
It quoted Klaus as saying after a meeting with Zeman, who heads the strong opposition party the Social Democrats, that he had dropped his objection to the chamber's investigation.
"It's clear that it is wise for this commission to start its work," CTK quoted Klaus as saying after a meeting with his political arch rival Zeman who has been pushing for the commission for weeks.

The decision took place under political pressure generated by August's failure of the medium-sized Kreditni Banka and Tuesday's decision by the central bank to place the largest fully-private bank Agrobanka a.s. under forced administration.

Five executives from Kreditni Banka have been indicted on fraud charges connected to a 2.88 billion crown debt swap scheme, and a special government commission of ministers has already been selected to conduct its own probe into Kreditni.

Both Kreditni, with losses totalling 12 billion crowns stemming from questionable loan practices, and Agrobanka, which became illiquid because of its connection to Kreditni, had strong ties to a secretive investment group called Motoinvest.
To date, the central bank has intervened in 12 troubled banks -- in a post-Communist banking sector which once numbered nearly 60 banks -- several of which have been shut.

Zeman, whose party's strong showing in June elections stripped Klaus's ruling coalition of its parliamentary majority, said the probe should look at the Kreditni case and search for legislation to improve the entire banking sector.

"A warning for foreign investors is the state of the banking system itself. It is not the crash of 11 banks, but the fact that at least 10 of them were never fully investigated," Zeman told a news conference before meeting Klaus.
"This is a jungle which pretends to be our economics, he added."
